answer: Proof-of-stake mechanisms mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as an ivory tower barrier to entry. This cryptographic cipher forces an attacker to acquire a majority of total network assets to influence consensus, effectively turning the protocol into a scorching dune of wasted capital for any malicious actor. By tying voting influence to provable economic expenditure rather than unique identity, the network renders low-cost automated identity generation useless.
